The Barsen'thor represents the playable Jedi Consular character from the [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] on [[December 20]], [[2011]].<ref name="TORRelease">{{TORweb|url=info/news/news-article/20111014-1|text=Global Launch for The Old Republic}}</ref> The storyline of the Consular character was written by [[Joanna Berry]]<ref name="Joanna Berry" /> with [[Daniel Erickson]] serving as the lead writer on the entire project, responsible for overall story and for maintaining consistency between the classes.<ref name="Daniel Erickson">{{WebCite|url=http://pc.gamespy.com/articles/121/1215532p1.html|text=GameSpy: Dialogue Wheel: We Interrogate Star Wars: The Old Republic's Lead Writer &ndash; Page 1|author=Stapleton, Dan|date=2012-12-29|work=[[Wikipedia:GameSpy|GameSpy]]|archivedate=20120108014917}}</ref>

[[File:The_Old_Republic_cover.png|thumb|right|250px|The Jedi Consular is one of the eight playable character classes in the MMO ''Star Wars: The Old Republic''.]]
According to Berry, the main goal of the Consular storyline was to explore how the Jedi faced the dark side of the Force, how they used their power and wisdom and not only lightsaber skills, and how they strove to serve the Republic. The main element of the story was mystery and the quest for truth, using intelligence and courage to achieve the goal. Berry compared the Consular's journey to the growth of the [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] character from the ''[[Star Wars]]'' film series. She also deliberately wrote many situations which forced the player to make difficult choices&mdash;choosing either what is morally right or what can help win the war with the Empire.<ref name="Joanna Berry" />

The male Consular is voiced by [[Nolan North]] and the female by [[Athena Karkanis]]. The character received a unique musical piece in ''The Old Republic'' that can be heard during gameplay<ref name="TOR" /> and was featured on the game's [[Star Wars: The Old Republic (soundtrack)|official soundtrack]] under the title "Peace, The Jedi Consular."<ref name="Soundtrack">[[Star Wars: The Old Republic (soundtrack)|''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' soundtrack]]</ref> This article only describes the events of the Consular storyline, not including any of the content which can be completed by members of any class: such as planetary quest-chains, sidequests, bonus quests, daily quest hubs, periodic game events, [[Wikipedia:Player versus player|PvP]] content, and on-rails space missions. Group content such as heroic missions, flashpoints, uprisings, and operations is also not described, since the group can consist of any combination of the four Republic classes, and in some cases, even a mix of Republic and Imperial characters.

The [[2013]] [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel|''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'']] digital expansion introduced Chapter Four of the class stories, with Republic characters being called by Chancellor Saresh to solve the [[Conquest of Makeb|crisis]] on the Hutt-occupied planet [[Makeb]]. However, the events of the expansion are the same for all four Republic classes&mdash;the Jedi Consular, the Jedi Knight, the [[Meteor (Havoc Squad)|Trooper]], and the [[Voidhound|Smuggler]]&mdash;with minor differences in dialogue. Since it has not been confirmed which of the four Republic classes participated in the mission to Makeb, the events of ''Rise of the Hutt Cartel'' are also omitted from this article.<ref name="RotHC">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''</ref>

The [[2014]] [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Galactic Starfighter|''Galactic Starfighter'']] and [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Galactic Strongholds|''Galactic Strongholds'']] expansions largely lacked story content and were focused on player-versus-player space combat<ref name="GSF">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Galactic Starfighter]]''</ref> and player housing, respectively.<ref name="GSH">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Galactic Strongholds]]''</ref> Later that year, another story-driven expansion, [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan|''Shadow of Revan'']], was released, comprising Chapter 5 of the game's characters' stories. Most of the expansion was once again the same for every class. However, each class was presented with one unique mission specific to their previous story, as well as a different ending cutscene conversation. As such, this article includes the unique class mission and assumes that the Barsen'thor participated in the fight on Yavin 4 in order to incorporate the unique ending. However, it refrains from mentioning the specifics of the other missions of the expansion.<ref name="SoR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan]]''</ref>

===Character identity and customization===
{{Quote|You're the "Barsen'thor," the Warden of the Jedi Order, right?|Tai Cordan, among other NPCs, addresses the player character as the Barsen'thor|<ref name="The Coalition" />}}
Since ''The Old Republic'' is largely a customizable game, many aspects of the Consular character, such as species, gender, name, and personality, are player determined. During the creation of the character, the following species are available initially: Human, [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]], Mirialan, Twi'lek, or Zabrak.<ref name="Getting Started">{{TORweb|url=info/newplayerguide/chapter-two|text=Getting Started|nolive=1}}</ref> Since Game Update 1.2: Legacy, four additional species&mdash;Cyborg, [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]], [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]], and [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith pureblood]]&mdash;can be unlocked by reaching level 50 with another character of that species.<ref name="Update 1.2">{{TORweb|url=gameupdates/1.2-legacy|text=Game Update 1.2: Legacy}}</ref> Finally, additional species options, such as [[Cathar/Legends|Cathar]] and [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]], can be purchased from the in-game Cartel Market.<ref name="TOR" /> Another customizable feature is the advanced class, which is mainly a gameplay mechanic and bears no influence on the storyline. Each of the advanced classes grants the Consular character access to different Force abilities, either increasing the character's damage (both classes), healing (Sages only), or defense (Shadows only).<ref name="Advanced Training: Jedi Consular" />

[[File:JediShadow-TOR.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A sample Jedi Consular from the ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' website]]
Therefore, the status of the Consular as a Sage or a Shadow cannot be determined. Due to the character name being chosen by each individual player, the Consular character is never referred to by name throughout the game except for in loading screens, which feature game summaries similar to the [[opening crawl]]s that appeared in the ''Star Wars'' films. As the player progresses through the class storyline, the summaries change to reflect the current events. The player-created name appears in these summaries, but not in any in-game voice material or written content.<ref name="TOR" />

After saving Hallow Voice in the mission "The Voice From The Tomb," the Jedi Consular player may choose between three Esh-Kha names: "Sky Hunter," "Ember Fist," and "Silent Teeth." Whichever the player chooses, Qyzen Fess, if present, would opine that it pleases the Scorekeeper, while Tharan Cedrax, if present, would comment that the Jedi is "going native." If Felix Iresso is present, he would express his liking for the name as it is easier to say than "Barsen'thor," and if Zenith is present, he would simply add that that was a "lot fuss for a code name."<ref name="The Voice From The Tomb" /> Hallow Voice would address the player by the chosen Esh-Kha name henceforth.<ref name="New Horizons">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Hallow Voice|New Horizons}}</ref>

The [[2012]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' included a two-page summary of the Consular storyline, accompanied by several screenshots. One image served to illustrate the Consular fighting Flesh Raiders on Tython. The Consular was depicted as a Human female, wielding a [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsaber]], which is used by the Jedi Shadow advanced class. Another image depicted the Consular as a Twi'lek during the confrontation with Lord Vivicar, and the third one depicted the Barsen'thor during a meeting with the Rift Alliance, wearing full armor with facial features fully obscured.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> One of the writers of the ''Encyclopedia'', [[Hall Hood]], stated via [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] that the images were not meant to be taken as canon,<ref name="Hood Twitter">{{Twitter|hallhood|status/256790273751932931|[[Hall Hood]]|date=2012-10-12|quote=@cadecalrayn Definitely not.|archivedate=20160115013136|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: @hallhood Hey, Mr. Hood, question: the Encyclopedia shows the Knight as a Miraluka male in all photos. Is this canon?}}</ref> and that "canonical" character identities were determined by each individual player.<ref name="Hood Twitter 2">{{Twitter|hallhood|status/256796592433139712|[[Hall Hood]]|date=2012-10-12|quote=@cadecalrayn As far as I'm concerned, the 'canonical' identities of player classes are determined solely by their individual players.|archivefile=File:HallHood-CanonPlayers-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: @hallhood Is that true for all classes? How about the Trooper? They're wearing a helmet in all three pictures.}}</ref>

In [[2015]], however, Hood's statement was contradicted with the publication of [[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]], a supplement to [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' [[Star Wars: Force and Destiny|''Star Wars'' roleplaying game]], which addressed the Barsen'thor by "he" and "him" pronouns. The Rulebook also established that the tomb belonging to a previously unidentified Jedi in the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', was, in fact, the resting place of the Barsen'thor. It therefore [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the character's first mention in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity to have been the ''Jedi Academy'' game.<ref name="Force and Destiny Rulebook" />

====Assumptions made in this article====
Based on the information outlined above, this article addresses the character by he/him pronouns and the title "Barsen'thor," which is awarded after the completion of Chapter One of the storyline, in place of his name.<ref name="Vivicar Awaits" /> The game features multiple choices that drive the character toward either the light side or the dark side. Although the outcome of the storyline remains largely the same regardless of the player's choices&mdash;Nalen Raloch is defeated, Terrak Morrhage is stopped and his plague is cured, the Rift Alliance stays with the Republic, all of the companions join the player's party, and the Children of the Emperor are defeated&mdash;many aspects of the story may vary depending on the player's actions.<ref name="TOR" />

Choosing dark side options can lead to Raloch and Vivicar being killed<ref name="TOR" />&mdash;the latter leading to deaths of dozens Jedi Masters connected to him<ref name="Casualty List">{{TORcite|type=message|Casualty List|Master Jaric Kaedan}}</ref>&mdash;Captain Valon evading justice and joining with the Barsen'thor, and the player killing Syo Bakarn/the First Son instead of redeeming him. Any of the afflicted Jedi in Chapter One, including Yuon Par, can also be killed instead of shielded. A dark-side character is also not given the seat on the Jedi Council, but is instead recognized for his displayed ruthless methods of command and is granted the title of [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]].<ref name="TOR" /> However, since the Consular is a Republic-allied character, this article [[Forum:CT:TOR and video game canon|assumes]] that the player always chooses options that result in maximum light side points, when available.

===Companions and romances===
{{Quote|Listen, listen. For us&mdash;for my people&mdash;marriage isn't&hellip;it's not just a ritual. It's something that changes, and grows. First, we make a promise. "All seasons, all worlds. Under stars, and earth. You, and I.''"<br />"''All seasons, all worlds. Under stars&hellip;and earth. You, and I, Nadia.''"<br />"''I never thought anyone would say those words to me. I love you. I know this is just the beginning for us.|Nadia Grell and the male Consular|<ref name="The Bond of Jedi" />}}
Throughout the course of the game, the player is joined by five storyline-related companions. The first, Qyzen Fess, is received on Tython near the end of the Prologue,<ref name="The Forge" /> and the second, Tharan Cedrax, joins after the events on Nar Shaddaa in Chapter One.<ref name="Shadow Town" /> The third, Zenith, joins at the end of the Balmorra storyline in Chapter 2,<ref name="Passing the Torch" /> and the fourth, Lieutenant Iresso, is acquired on Hoth.<ref name="Chasing the Legend" /> The fifth companion is Nadia Grell, who, despite joining the player's crew at the start of Chapter 2 as a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]],<ref name="An Alliance of Opposites" /> only becomes available for use as a companion after the mission to the ''Euphony'' at the end of the Belsavis quest line in Chapter Three.<ref name="Fearless" />

However, only one companion may accompany the player at any given time. For most of the game, the player can select the companion, with a few notable exceptions.<ref name="TOR" /> Qyzen Fess accompanies the player for the final two missions on Tython,<ref name="Rajivari's Legacy" /><ref name="The Forge" /> and all of the Chapter I missions until the final Nar Shaddaa quest, in which Tharan Cedrax is required as a companion.<ref name="Shadow Town" /> Zenith accompanies the player during the final mission on Balmorra,<ref name="Passing the Torch" /> while Nadia Grell is required for the mission to the ''Euphony''.<ref name="Fearless" />

[[File:Barsenthor_C2-N2.png|thumb|right|250px|C2-N2 is a Republic ship droid, which can be summoned as a companion.]]
Therefore, those missions aside, this article refrains from mentioning the Barsen'thor's companion, since it could have been either one. All of the companions with the exception of C2-N2 have over a dozen conversations which are unlocked as the player levels up and gains affection with each character. In addition to that, Qyzen Fess also has three companion missions,<ref name="TOR" /> taking place on Tatooine,<ref name="Shadow on the Sand" /> Alderaan,<ref name="Rebirth" /> and Taris,<ref name="Straight and Narrow" /> which detail the story of the hunt for Veneb Drassk.<ref name="TOR" />

Like any other character classes in the game, the Consular can also gain access to a number of other optional companions, such as the assassin droid [[HK-51 series assassin droid|HK-51]] and the female [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] mercenary [[Treek/Legends|Treek]], who can be obtained through optional recruitment quests. Other companions are available for purchase through the in-game Cartel Market<ref name="TOR" /> or given out during promotional events.<ref name="Master Ranos">{{TORweb|url=dark-vs-light/rewards|text=Dark vs. Light event}}</ref> An additional companion, the ship droid C2-N2, is acquired when the player receives a personal ship at the end of the Coruscant storyline; the droid's participation in the story is limited to comments made each time the player returns to the ship.<ref name="Ancient Secrets" /> Although it is possible to use those optional companions, including the ship droid, during gameplay portions of the Jedi Consular storyline in the game,<ref name="TOR" /> this article treats their usage as a non-storyline gameplay mechanic.

The male character can romance Nadia Grell by selecting flirt-related responses during their conversations. If the character is female, however, Felix Iresso can be romanced instead. Both romances may culminate in the marriage of the player character and the respective companion. The romanced companion also sends the player several love letters afterward. In those letters, Nadia talks about how her dreams have gotten better,<ref name="Dreams">{{TORcite|type=message|Dreams|Nadia Grell}}</ref> sends the Consular some gifts from Sarkhai,<ref name="A Package from Sarkhai">{{TORcite|type=message|A Package from Sarkhai|Nadia Grell}}</ref> and contemplates that the Jedi Order's ban on marriage might be wrong.<ref name="Thinking">{{TORcite|type=message|Thinking|Nadia Grell}}</ref> Iresso tells the Consular that he keeps thinking of her,<ref name="For you">{{TORcite|type=message|For you|Felix Iresso}}</ref> invites her to watch a [[Holovid/Legends|holovid]], [[Squad 223: Mission Zero]], he remembers from his youth,<ref name="Something to share">{{TORcite|type=message|Something to share|Felix Iresso}}</ref> and tells her about a call he has received from a Jedi Master on Tython, who was asking about the Barsen'thor.<ref name="A Call from Tython">{{TORcite|type=message|A Call from Tython|Felix Iresso}}</ref>

Female characters can also have a flirtatious relationship with Tharan Cedrax<ref name="A Holiday from Hutta" /> that can culminate in a sexual encounter between the two.<ref name="Message in a Bottle">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Tharan Cedrax|Message in a Bottle}}</ref> However, Cedrax chooses not to pursue the relationship further.<ref name="Genius Will Out">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Tharan Cedrax|Genius Will Out}}</ref>

===Cut content===
Several text files within ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} game files contain mentions of a mission that was supposed to take the Consular to the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] early in Chapter One. Taking place at some point after the events on Coruscant but before the mission to Tatooine, the mission was supposed to have involved the Consular investigating Vivicar's presence on the planet. According to unused conversation files with Syo Bakarn, the mission would have somehow involved an individual named [[Kellian Zell]].<ref name="TOR files">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' game files</ref>

However, none of that content made it into the final version of the Consular story, and the character never visits Ord Mantell in the finished game. According to the files, another major plot point was cut from the final game: during the Battle of Corellia, the First Son was originally going to contact the Barsen'thor, informing the Jedi about an Imperial fleet he had dispatched to conquer Sarkhai. In response, Nadia was supposed to leave to defend her homeworld, temporarily locking her out as a companion. The Consular's alignment choices would have then determined the ease at which the Sarkhai repelled the attack, either making it an easy victory for Nadia's people or a hard-fought one.<ref name="TOR files" />

===''Knights of the Fallen Empire'' and merging of the character stories===
{{Main|Alliance Commander}}
The 2015 digital expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] condensed the game's eight storylines into a single one, establishing that the Barsen'thor&mdash;as well as the other character classes&mdash;disappeared around the time of the Eternal Empire's invasion of the galaxy.<ref name="KotFE 1" /> Regardless of their class, the player in ''Knights of the Fallen Empire'' reemerges five years later as a veteran of the Galactic War known only as [[Alliance Commander|the Outlander]]<ref name="KotFE 3" />&mdash;later known as "the Commander" of the Eternal Alliance<ref name="KOTFEChapter9">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=9}}</ref>&mdash;while the other seven classes are still considered missing.<ref name="KotFE 3" />

Since it has not been confirmed within the ''Star Wars'' Legends continuity which one of the eight playable classes is the Commander, this article treats the Barsen'thor as missing in action during the events of the expansion and all story content of ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' released afterward. All events related to the main character in ''Knights of the Fallen Empire'' and onward are detailed in the Commander article.
